item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, leaning negative. I found a few concrete 2024 examples of Erdoğan speaking candidly or at least consistently with later reporting, but the stronger pattern is a controlled information environment, repeated terrorism-framing of opponents, and little direct evidence of a general habit of strict truthfulness when power or reputation was at stake.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports | [After huge setback in local elections, which way forward now for Turkey's Erdogan?](https://apnews.com/article/08b72132244340176a3ef52e6d2da6ff) | AP | 2024-04-01 | https://apnews.com/article/08b72132244340176a3ef52e6d2da6ff | Erdoğan acknowledged his party had suffered a “loss of altitude” and said it would engage in self-criticism. That is a real public admission of defeat rather than an obvious denial designed to protect prestige. | 7B.1 |
| Supports | [Turkey's Erdogan offers to help end Russia-Ukraine war; Kremlin rules him out as intermediary](https://theprint.in/world/turkeys-erdogan-offers-to-help-end-russia-ukraine-war-kremlin-rules-him-out-as-intermediary/2159619/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-07-04 | https://theprint.in/world/turkeys-erdogan-offers-to-help-end-russia-ukraine-war-kremlin-rules-him-out-as-intermediary/2159619/ | Erdoğan told Putin Ankara could help end the war, and the Kremlin’s pushback was about his role as intermediary, not the basic existence of his offer. This is consistent with a straightforward public statement, not a visible fabrication. | 7B.1 |
| Supports | [Turkey wants deeper ties with Egypt on natural gas, nuclear energy](https://theprint.in/world/erdogan-says-turkey-wants-deeper-ties-with-egypt-on-natural-gas-nuclear-energy/2253082/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-09-04 | https://theprint.in/world/erdogan-says-turkey-wants-deeper-ties-with-egypt-on-natural-gas-nuclear-energy/2253082/ | Erdoğan framed nuclear energy as civilian cooperation with Egypt, not weapons or coercive nuclear signaling. That is weak but relevant evidence that he sometimes used plain, non-deceptive framing on sensitive subjects. | 7B.1 |
| Cuts against | [Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says Erdoğan repeatedly accused legitimate opponents of supporting terrorism during the campaign, while state-run media heavily favored the AKP and the government restricted speech after the earthquake and during elections. That is strong evidence of misleading public messaging and a distorted information environment. | 7B.1, 6B.8, 6B.9 |
| Cuts against | [Turkey | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report describes continued tight media control, disproportionate airtime for incumbents, and regulator fines on critical outlets. That does not prove every statement was false, but it does show a system built to manage perception rather than maximize truthfulness. | 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.8 |
| Cuts against | [DMM says the claim "Erdoğan called Israel" was false](https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/gundem/dmm-cumhurbaskani-erdogan-israili-aradi-iddiasiyla-servis-edilen-haberleri-yalanladi/3438110) | Anadolu Agency / Presidency communications office | 2024-12-30 | https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/gundem/dmm-cumhurbaskani-erdogan-israili-aradi-iddiasiyla-servis-edilen-haberleri-yalanladi/3438110 | Erdoğan’s communications office had to deny a false report that he had called Israeli officials. This is only indirect evidence, but it reinforces that 2024 featured a lot of narrative management around Erdoğan rather than clean transparency. | 7B.1 |

**Search gap:** I did not find a clean 2024 mainstream fact-check showing Erdoğan himself directly lied to the legislature, courts, or allies in a single, high-confidence incident. The best negative evidence was systemic: media capture, selective terrorism accusations, and repeated official rebuttals around misleading stories.
